statement: Iron Knob quarried for 1,600 ft along strike, maximum width 220 ft; long and narrow, strikes north-south
Iron Monarch roughly circular in plan, 2,100 ft north-south by 2,200 ft east-west; benches to about 350 ft below the crest
Iron Monarch reserves computed from the 1,154 ft summit to the 540 ft level (drill hole bottom), with extension likely
Iron Prince: not a single mass but a series of lenticular bodies interfingered with banded iron formation and schist
Twelve named high-grade bodies along the Middleback Range (Monarch, Knob, Prince, Baron, Duke, Duchess, Knight, Chieftain, Queen, Count, Warrior, South Queen)
reading: 12 bodies over about 60 km of range

statement: High-grade reserves per body 47,000 to 59,376,000 tons; total 176,430,000 tons
Low-grade banded iron formation 5,430,000,000 tons over the North and South Middleback Ranges, Katunga Hills and Camel Hill line
reading: 5.4 Gt, ranges tens of km long

statement: Ore is high-grade hematite or martite with some residual magnetite; 60 to 68% Fe
Specific gravity of hard ore determined as 4.62; 4.5 taken as general average; a long ton occupies 8 cubic feet in situ
Lower-grade ore reckoned at 9 to 12 cubic feet to the ton
Mineral specific gravities: magnetite 5.0-5.1, hematite 4.9-5.3 (crystals 4.5-5.3), limonite 4.0-4.4
Hematite itself is almost non-magnetic, limonite only slightly; ore-body magnetic effects come from included magnetite particles; Iron Prince ore gives just over 1,000 gammas vertical intensity
Over the hematite quartzite (banded iron formation) anomalies of up to 8,000 gammas; unoxidised magnetite at 200-300 ft depth
Uptilted hematite quartzite strata give peaks over 50,000 gammas locally
Where the magnetite is sufficiently oxidised there may be no anomaly at all
Ore bodies occupy the keels of synclines in banded iron formation in the Middleback Group basement, replacing the banded iron formation; flanked by granitic schists
